title: Companion 1.2.0-rc.2 on the tour's dLive: the 1.2.0 submission check (desk list B2) -- written to be run by the operator alone
version: 2026-11-24 draft 3 (Dev: Bitfocus Companion module, for the UK rehearsal days 26-27 Nov; module 1.2.0-rc.2, Console Bridge 1.5.0-beta.5). Draft 3 rewrites every step for the operator running it with nobody in chat: each one says what to type and what its pass line is. It also re-cuts the candidate as rc.2, because rc.1 predates the feedback fix that ships on 3 Dec, and corrects two checks in draft 2's step 2 that could not have passed as written (the module id is dylanmaudio-apps, not console_bridge, and /api/connections carries no version field at all).

the module at 5017d29 on build/sr-1.2.0 (1.2.0-rc.2); CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section

tests.title: Companion 1.2.0-rc.2 on the tour's dLive -- about 8 minutes, almost all of it over HTTP, operator alone
tests.answers: the module thread, before the 3 Dec submission: is everything 1.2.0 added since the last real dLive (4 Nov) invisible on a dLive? The console gate, the forgotten-value rule, the fade-ack warnings and the rename.
tests.expect: The gate is silent: no refusal line of any kind in Companion's log. Every write lands and reads back. A fade that lands warns about nothing. After a recall the strip variables are stale, never empty. scene_current survives a connection toggle (#342). The cold state agrees with the surface, with the stereo trio empty, which is a dLive's right answer. And the scene list's indexing is read before any recall: a slot number is a place on a dLive, which no run so far could show, because the shop's test show used slots 1 and 2.
tests.safety: This is the tour's show desk, not a test desk, but it is the operator's alone from load-in to load-out (S10, 24 Nov). WRITES (steps 7, 8 and 9b) go in the couple of hours before the PA is connected; outside that window mute your own system controller first. The show is a test show if one is loaded, otherwise a COPY of the main show -- never the show itself. Every write is on ONE input you name in step 3 as having no source, no output patch and no main assign; if you cannot name one, answer 'read-only' and the block runs its reading half alone, which is still a pass for that half. Scene recalls happen only on places you name, and you put the desk back at the surface. The module under test runs on the MacBook Pro; the Mac Mini is OFF THE NETWORK for the run. CONNECTIONS TO THE MIXRACK, which allows four: Console Bridge takes one, and the runner itself opens ONE more on 51325 when started with --host (this protocol asks for a single client). No step in this block sends anything on the runner's connection -- it exists so the session is recorded as a live run rather than a rehearsal. If the desk is already at its limit, quit Director first.

steps.prompt:
SET UP, on the MacBook Pro, before you go near the desk. The Mac Mini is off the network for this run, so nothing here touches the show machine.
  (a) INSTALL THE MODULE. Companion -> Modules -> 'Import module package' -> pick 'Companion Module 1.2.0-rc.2.tgz' from Latest Builds/Betas. It is the button that says 'Import module package', NOT 'Import offline module bundle' below it.
  (b) PIN IT. Connections tab -> the console_bridge row -> the pencil by Module Version -> choose v1.2.0-rc.2 -> Save.
  (c) CHECK THE PORT. Still on that connection: the Console Bridge port must be 8765, the installed app's. On 24 Nov this machine's connection was pointed at 8770 (a test rig that is not running) and the row read 'Waiting for Console Bridge at 127.0.0.1:8770 (info 404)'. If you see 8770, change it to 8765 and Save, or every step below fails.
  (d) LOG LEVEL. That connection's log level -> Debug. Steps 4 and 8 read the log file.
  (e) GET THE TEST PAGE and import it. In Terminal:
      git -C ~/Documents/GitHub/companion-module-dylanmaudio show 5017d29:blocks/shop-check.companionconfig > ~/Desktop/b2-page.companionconfig
    then Companion -> Buttons -> Import -> ~/Desktop/b2-page.companionconfig, onto PAGE 11. It carries 14 buttons: row 0 a channel's fader and mute, row 1 scenes by place, row 2 scenes by number. It was written for the shop's show, where Input 9 was safe and the scenes were ours. NEITHER IS TRUE ON THE TOUR'S DESK. Step 3 settles which input is safe; row 0's five buttons must then be re-pointed at it (Buttons -> page 11 -> each button -> its action's Input number) before anything is pressed. Leave rows 1 and 2 alone until step 9.
  (f) THE CONNECTION'S NAME. Every command below says console_bridge, which is what the bridge connection is called on your Companion since 24 Nov. The name is both the variable prefix and the URL path, so if this machine calls it something else, substitute that name everywhere below.
PASS: the Connections tab shows console_bridge, Module Version 1.2.0-rc.2, port 8765, and page 11 has its 14 buttons.
RECORD HERE: anything you had to change to get that.

steps.text:
THE BUILD -- nothing is sent to the desk. Three commands in Terminal.
  (a) ls ~/Library/Application\ Support/companion/modules/ | grep dylanmaudio-apps
      PASS: a line reading dylanmaudio-apps-1.2.0-rc.2. The module's id is dylanmaudio-apps; console_bridge is only the connection's name, so do not grep for it.
  (b) shasum -a 256 ~/Documents/GitHub/dLive-Utility-Apps-Builds/Latest\ Builds/Betas/Companion\ Module\ 1.2.0-rc.2.tgz
      PASS: 4bdb5286c9be066e7297a6eeae64dc529c9d5435dff341a4460b330597294989
      FAIL: any other digest -- someone cut a different build under the same name. STOP and say so; do not carry on.
  (c) On Companion's Connections tab, read the Module Version column on the console_bridge row with your eyes.
      PASS: 1.2.0-rc.2. (Draft 2 asked for this over the API. Companion's /api/connections returns only id, label, moduleId, enabled and status -- there is no version field to read, which is why this one is done by eye.)
  ALSO RECORD: Console Bridge's own version, from its menu-bar About (wants 1.5.0-beta.5).

steps.question: Three things before any write. (a) Is this a test show, or a copy of the main show, rather than the show itself? (b) Is the PA disconnected, or have you muted your system controller? (c) Can you name an input that is safe to write to -- no source patched, no output patched, no main assign? Answer 'all three answered' only if all three are true, and write the input number in the next note. If you cannot name a safe input, answer 'read-only': the block then skips steps 7, 8 and 9b, and the reading half still counts.

steps.text:
THE CONSOLE GATE MUST BE INVISIBLE HERE -- nothing is sent. This is the main reason the block exists: 1.2.0 added a per-console gate for the seven families that are not the dLive, and on a dLive it must do absolutely nothing.
  (a) curl -s 127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1/info | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin).get("console"), indent=1))'
      PASS: the block names the dLive, and there is NO verified_on_desk key in it at all. Absence is what means 'verified on the dLive', so an absent key is the pass.
  (b) grep -c -e 'has not been checked against one' -e "isn't sent on a" "$HOME/Library/Application Support/companion/logs/companion-$(date +%F).0.log"
      PASS: 0.
      FAIL: any number above 0. One of those lines on a dLive is a fail whatever else passes -- copy the whole line out and stop.
  If the grep says 'No such file or directory', the log for today has not been written yet: press any button on page 11 once and try again.

THE CONNECTION'S OWN WORDS -- nothing is sent.
  curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/connections | python3 -c 'import json,sys; rows=json.load(sys.stdin); rows=rows.values() if isinstance(rows,dict) else rows; print([r["status"] for r in rows if r["label"]=="console_bridge"])'
  PASS: category 'ok'.
  FAIL: 'error' or 'warning'. If the message mentions port 8770, go back to step 1(c).
  RECORD the message string word for word -- it is the sentence an operator reads on the Connections tab, and its wording is part of what is being checked.

steps.prompt:
THE COLD STATE, read over HTTP -- nothing is sent. There is no answer key on this desk: THE SURFACE IS THE ANSWER.
  First pick two inputs you can see on the surface and note what they are called and where one of them sits. Put their numbers in A and B below, and a channel you know is STEREO-LINKED in S. Then paste this one line:
    A=9; B=12; S=1; for v in name_ch$A name_ch$B fader_ch$A mute_ch$B scene_current scene_current_name connected gets_missed unsupported_gets linked_ch$S partner_ch$S width_ch$S; do printf '%s = %s\n' "$v" "$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/console_bridge/$v/value)"; done
  PASS, line by line:
    name_ch$A, name_ch$B      the names as the surface shows them
    fader_ch$A                the level the surface shows, within 0.2 dB
    mute_ch$B                 true or false, as the surface shows
    scene_current             the scene the desk is on
    scene_current_name        EMPTY IS A PASS unless a dLive show file has been imported into the module. Empty here is expected, not a fault.
    connected                 true
    gets_missed               0, or a small number that is not growing
    unsupported_gets          EXPECTED NON-EMPTY on 1.2.0 if any assign, HPF, preamp or send-level feedback is on a button anywhere: it names the ops the bridge has no mirror for, and saying so is new in this release. Empty is also fine if no such feedback is placed. Copy whatever it says.
    linked_ch$S, partner_ch$S, width_ch$S   ALL THREE EMPTY IS THE PASS. A dLive cannot report an input's link, and empty is how the module says 'cannot say'. The fail here is the word false.
  RECORD HERE: paste the whole output, and beside it what the surface showed.

steps.text:
THE WRITES. SKIP THIS STEP ENTIRELY if step 3 said read-only.
Everything here is on the input you named, inside the PA-off window or with your system controller muted, and only after row 0's buttons have been re-pointed at that input (step 1e). Put N below to that input's number.
  N=9; for b in 0 1 3 4 2; do curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/0/$b/press; sleep 2; printf 'after button %s: fader=%s mute=%s\n' "$b" "$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/console_bridge/fader_ch$N/value)" "$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/console_bridge/mute_ch$N/value)"; done
  The five buttons in that order are: -20 dB, 0 dB, MUTE on, MUTE off, -inf.
  PASS: fader reads about -20, then about 0, then MUTE true, then MUTE false, then -inf. Every one must land: a dLive is not a foreign family, so the module converts dB to the desk's own scale itself, and a refusal here is a real fail.
  NOTE: the press endpoint answers 204 whether or not a button is there, so a 204 proves nothing. The read-back above is the proof.
  THEN PUT THE FADER BACK where you found it, by hand at the surface if the -inf press is not where it started.

THE FADE, which is new in this release. Skip if read-only. WHAT IS BEING CHECKED IS THE LOG, not the fader.
  (a) Companion -> Buttons -> page 11, a spare key -> add the module's 'Fader level' action on your safe input, target -10 dB, fade time 3000 ms. Save.
  (b) Press it. Wait 4 s. Then: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/console_bridge/fader_ch$N/value -- wants about -10.
  (c) Press it again, and while it is still moving press it once more with a different target. Let it finish.
  (d) grep -nE 'warn' "$HOME/Library/Application Support/companion/logs/companion-$(date +%F).0.log" | tail -20
  PASS: the fade that landed wrote NO warning. The fade cut short by the second press wrote at most an info line.
  FAIL: a warning from an ordinary press that landed. This is the one thing in 1.2.0 that could nag an operator all night, so copy any warning out in full.

SCENES. Part (a) is read-only and must be done FIRST, before any recall.
  (a) WHICH INDEX IS A 'PLACE' ON THIS DESK?
      curl -s 127.0.0.1:8765/api/v1/state | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print([k for k in d.get("state",d) if k.startswith("scene.") and k.endswith(".name")][:40])'
      On a dLive the bridge recalls a scene BY PLACE and refuses a scene number outright, and the console block gives first 1, last 500. So a scene stored in slot 201 should appear as scene.201.name. If instead it appears as scene.14.name -- the 14th stored scene -- then a place counts stored scenes and every number in this block must be read that way.
      WRITE DOWN WHICH IT IS BEFORE PRESSING ANYTHING. Every run so far used slots 1 and 2, where the two readings agree, so this is the first time the difference can be seen, and a recall of the wrong scene on a show desk is the one mistake this block must not make.
  (b) WHAT A RECALL LEAVES BEHIND. Skip if read-only, or if no scene is safe to recall.
      Pick two scenes that are safe to recall on this copy, note which PLACE each sits at, and re-point page 11 row 1's first two buttons at those places. Then:
        curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/location/11/1/0/press
        sleep 5
        A=9; B=12; for v in scene_current name_ch$A mute_ch$B fader_ch$A; do printf '%s = %s\n' "$v" "$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/console_bridge/$v/value)"; done
      PASS: scene_current is the place you recalled, and the three strip variables still hold their OLD values. Stale is correct on a dLive -- the bridge keeps the pre-recall values until something asks again, and that is the design today.
      FAIL: any of the three EMPTY. 1.2.0 un-learns a value the bridge reports as unknown, which is right on an Avantis and must never happen on a dLive. Empty, not stale, is the fail here.
      Then recall the second scene the same way, and put the desk back on the scene it was on when you arrived -- that one at the surface, by hand.

THE LOADED SCENE ON CONNECT (#342). This only works if the desk is NOT sitting on the first scene in the list, so do it after step 9b, or recall something at the surface first.
  (a) In Companion's Connections tab, toggle the console_bridge connection OFF, wait, and ON again. Give it about 5 s. A Console Bridge restart does NOT test this -- the module keeps its state across a reconnect, so it has to be the connection.
  (b) BEFORE pressing any button: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/variable/console_bridge/scene_current/value
  PASS: it reads the loaded scene's place.
  FAIL: 0, blank, or 1. That is #342 still unfixed.
  RECORD it either way -- this one is worth knowing even when it passes.

steps.question: On Companion's Connections tab, is the console_bridge row green/OK -- not Connecting, and no error?
Press page 11's 'MUTE on' button for your safe input: does the button itself go red while that input is muted, and back when you press 'MUTE off'? Skip if the block ran read-only.
